questions.question: Which of the following indicates the system introduced by Lord Cornwallis granting legal ownership of land to the zamindars in Bengal in order to get a fixed revenue by a fixed date?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Permanent Settlement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Permanent Settlement system**, also known as the **Zamindari system**, was implemented by **Lord Cornwallis in 1793** to **confer legal ownership of land to zamindars in Bengal.**
 
• Under this arrangement, zamindars were designated **as the landowners**, and an agreement was reached between the company and the zamindars to fix the land revenue.
 
• In this system, the government retained **10/11th of the total land revenue collected **by the zamindars, while the remaining portion was retained by the zamindars themselves.
 
• The Permanent Settlement system was predominantly observed in regions such as **West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• It provided zamindars with perpetual land rights, without stipulating fixed rent or occupancy rights for actual cultivators. Consequently, zamindars were tasked with collecting land revenue from the farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ryotwari system,** introduced in 1820 in British India, was a land revenue system.
 
• **The ****Mahalwari system**, introduced in 1822 by Holt Mackenzie, was a land revenue system.
 
• **The Taluqdari System** was developed as a fiscal policy and a zamindari management technique.

questions.question: Under whose rule did the Mughal empire achieve its largest territorial limits?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__

__
 
• **Aurangzeb** was the sixth Mughal Emperor, ruling over most of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• His reign lasted from 1658 to 1707, making him one of the longest-reigning Mughal emperors.
 
• Under his rule, the Mughal Empire achieved its largest territorial extent, covering nearly the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• He was known for his military conquests and administrative reforms, which helped expand and consolidate the empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Akbar**, known as Akbar the Great, significantly expanded the Mughal Empire and established a centralized administrative system.
 
• The Mughal Empire began to decline shortly after Aurangzeb's death, leading to the eventual establishment of British colonial rule in India.

questions.question: Shivaji, the famous Maratha warrior fought against who among the following Mughal Emperors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Maratha ruler, Shivaji carved out the independent Maratha Kingdom in the territories of north and south Konkan.
 
• To contain the spread of the Maratha empire,** Aurangzeb annexed Bijapur** in 1686 AD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chhatrapati Shivaji was a great** Maratha ruler **who carved out his own independent kingdom and layed the groundwork for the Maratha Empire.
 
• In **1648,** Shivaji occupied the **fort of Purandergarh.**
 
• This provided an impregnable defence to the Marathas in the years to come.
 
• The next in line to fall was the** fort of Javli in 1656**.
 
• It was the stronghold of the famous **Mavle chieftain Chandra Rao More**.
 
• With its occupation, he got another stronghold over Raigarh which was to assume the status of the Maratha capital shortly after.
 
• The **conquest of Javli** not only opened the gate for further expansion towards south and west Konkan but it also increased Shivaji's military strength with Mavle chieftains of More territory joining him.
 
• In 1659 he **killed Afzal Khan**, a notable general of Bijapur.
 
• In 1663 he wounded and chased away the **Mughal general and Aurangzeb’s uncle Shaista Khan.**
 
• To cap these bold acts, he audaciously directed his soldiers t**o plunder Surat (1664),** the major Mughal port on the Arabian Sea.
 
• After Shivaji plundered Surat, Aurangzeb swung into action and sent an army under the command of a **Rajput general, Raja Jai Singh **who was ordered to destroy Shivaji and annex Bijapur. 
 
• Raja Jai Singh succeeded in **defeating Shivaji at Purandar (1665).**
 
• Shivaji signed the** Treaty of Purander in 1665** with Raja Jai Singh.

questions.question: When was Khandesh merged into the Mughal empire by Akbar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1601**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1601, Mughal Emperor Akbar **incorporated **Khandesh **into the** Mughal empire.**
 
• Khandesh had been under the rule of the **Farooqi dynasty **since **1382**, established by **Malik Ahmad.**
 
• Akbar's conquest involved occupying Burhanpur in 1599 and besieging Asirgarh Fort, which he successfully took on January 17, 1601.
 
• Despite resistance from the ruler of the Khandesh Sultanate, Miran Bahadur Shah, Akbar appointed Prince Daniyal to oversee the newly established Subahs of Ahmadnagar, Berar, and Khandesh.
 
• Akbar had initiated administrative reforms in 1572, creating the first twelve subahs, which included Kabul, Lahore, Multan, Delhi, Agra, Avadh, Illahabad, Bihar, Bangal, Malwa, Ajmer, and Gujarat.
 
• Following his conquest of the Deccan, Akbar further expanded his administrative divisions, establishing three additional subahs: Berar, Khandesh, and Ahmadnagar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Abu'l-Fath Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar, **widely recognized as **Akbar the Great**, was the **third Mughal emperor**, reigning from **1556 to 1605.**
 
• Akbar ascended to the throne after his father, Humayun, and was initially supported by a regent,
 
• Bairam Khan, who aided in expanding and consolidating Mughal territories in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Under Akbar's rule, Mughal India experienced significant economic growth, tripling in both size and wealth, which facilitated commercial expansion and fostered the flourishing of an Indo-Persian culture.
 
• Following Akbar's reign, his son, Prince Salim, later known as Jahangir, succeeded him as emperor.

questions.question: In which of these battles the involvement of the Mughal army was **not** there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Battle of Aliwal.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• It redounded in a decisive British palm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Battle of Haldighati:**

 
 
• The Battle of Haldighati was a battle fought on 18 June 1576 between the armies of the Rana of Mewar, Maharana Pratap, and the Mughal emperor Akbar’s forces, led by Man Singh I of Amber.
 
• Although the battle ended in defeat for the forces of Mewar, Maharana Pratap escaped continuing his valiant resistance against the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Buxar:**
 
 
• The Battle of Buxar took place in 1764, in the town of Buxar in present-day Bihar, India. It was a significant battle fought during the British East India Company's expansion in India.
 
• The British East India Company, led by Major Hector Munro, faced a coalition of Indian rulers consisting of the Nawab of Oudh, Shuja-ud-Daula, the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, and the forces of the ruler of Mir Qasim.
 
• The battle was the outcome of the misuse of Farman and Dastak, and also the trade expansionist aspiration of the English.
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Panipat:**
 
 
• The Hindu ruler Samrat Hem Chandra Vikramaditya, often known as Hemu, governed North India from Delhi, and the army of Akbar fought the Second Battle of Panipat.
 
• On November 5, 1556, it took place. Hemu had just captured the provinces of Delhi and Agra in the Battle of Delhi, beating the Mughals led by Tardi Beg Khan, and named himself Raja Vikramaditya during a coronation in Purana Quila in Delhi.
 
• When Akbar and his guardian Bairam Khan learned of the loss of Agra and Delhi, they marched to Panipat to reclaim the domains.
 
• The two armies met in Panipat, not far from the site of the 1556 Second Battle of Panipat. The generals of Akbar achieved a tremendous victory.

questions.question: In the Delhi Sultanate, which of the following were known as Bandagan?

options.text: Special person appointed for religious conversion
Special Officer for Land Revenue Recovery
Specialized artisans employed in the royal kharkhanas
Special slaves bought for military service

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Special slaves bought for military service.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• During the Sultanate period, special **slaves purchased for military service** were called Bandagan in Persian.
 
• A large empire like the Delhi Sultanate needed trustworthy governors and bureaucrats to consolidate. The early Delhi Sultans, especially **Iltutmish**, preferred their special slaves recruited for military duty, known as bandagan in Persian, rather than installing aristocrats and landed chieftains as administrators.
 
• To fill some of the most **significant political positions** in the kingdom, they **underwent thorough training**. The Sultan could count on them since they were fully reliant on his lord.
 
• The **Khaljis and Tughluqs kept using bandagan **and promoted people from lowly backgrounds, who were frequently their clients, to positions of prominence in politics.
 
• They were chosen to serve as governors and generals. But this also added a **component of political unpredictability.**
 
• Clients and slaves were **devoted to their patrons and masters but not to their heirs**. The New Sultans had their own slaves. As a result, when a new monarch came into power, the old and new nobility frequently clashed.
 
• Many elites were surprised by the Delhi Sultans' indulgence of these lowly people, and the Persian Tawarikh authors criticized the Delhi Sultans for elevating the "poor and base-born" to positions of power.

questions.question: Which ruler of the Chahamana dynasty made Ajmer his capital?

__
 
• **Ajayaraja Chahamana:-**

 
 
• He was an Indian king who ruled the Shakambhari Chahamana dynasty from 1113 to 1143 CE.
 
• **He is best known for establishing Ajmer as his capital city, a strategic move that enhanced the Chahamana kingdom's prominence in northwestern India. **
 
• Ajayaraja's reign was marked by military successes, including victories against the neighboring Ghaznavid empire.
 
• He also patronized the arts and religion, commissioning the construction of temples and promoting cultural activities.
 
• Ajayaraja's legacy as a powerful and astute ruler has secured his place in Indian history. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prithviraj**:-

 
 
• He was a ruler of the Chahamana dynasty who ruled from 1177 to 1192 CE.
 
• He is best known for his defeat of the Ghurid army led by Muhammad Ghori at the Battle of Tarain in 1191 CE.
 
• However, Ghori returned with a larger army in 1192 CE and defeated Prithviraj at the Second Battle of Tarain. Prithviraj was captured and executed, and his death marked the beginning of the Islamic conquest of India.
 
 
 
• 
 **Arnoraj**:-

 
 
• 
 He was a ruler of the Chahamana dynasty who ruled from 1135 to 1150 CE.
 
 
• 
 He is best known for his defeat of the Ghaznavid army led by Ghaznavid general Bahram Shah in 1136 CE.
 
 
• 
 Arnoraj also constructed the Anasagar Lake in Ajmer, which is still one of the largest man-made lakes in India.

questions.question: Shore temple of Mamallapuram was built by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pallavas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Shore temple of Mamallapuram:-**

__
 
• **It is a majestic granite monument located in Mamallapuram, India, stands as a testament to the architectural brilliance of the Pallava dynasty.**
 
• **Constructed during the 8th century AD, the temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a captivating example of Dravidian architecture.**
 
• The Shore Temple's grandeur lies in its intricate carvings, towering structures, and harmonious blend of religious and secular themes.
 
• The temple complex consists of three shrines, each dedicated to a Hindu deity: the main shrine to Shiva, a shrine to Vishnu, and a shrine to the goddess Durga.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Chalukya dynasty:-**

 
• **It ruled over parts of southern India from the 6th to the 12th centuries AD. **
 
• They were known for their architectural achievements, including the Badami Chalukya style, characterized by intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• They also made significant contributions to literature and patronized scholars and poets.

**Nagas:-**

 
• **These were a diverse group of tribes that ruled over parts of northern and central India from the 3rd century BC to the 14th century AD. **
 
• They were known for their distinctive sculptural style, characterized by serpent motifs and stylized human figures.
 
• They also played a significant role in the development of Buddhism in India.

**Chola dynasty:-**

 
• **They ruled over parts of southern India from the 9th to the 13th centuries AD. **
 
• They were a powerful maritime empire that controlled trade routes and established colonies in Southeast Asia.
 
• They were also known for their architectural achievements, including the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur and the Chola bronze sculptures.

questions.question: Which Bahmani ruler granted the title of 'Chief of the Merchants' or Malikut-Tujjar to Mahmud Gawan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• One of the most important personalities in the **Bahamani kingdom was Mahmud Gawan under whom, the Bahmani kingdom reached its peak.**
 
• **Mahmud Gawan**’s early life is obscure and was an** Iranian by birth and first reached Deccan as a trader.**
 
• He was granted the title of** ‘Chief of the Merchants’ or Malik-ut-Tujjar **by the Bahamani ruler, Humayun Shah.
 
• The sudden death of **Humayun **led to the coronation of his** minor son Ahmad III.**
 
• A regency council was set for the administration and** Mahmud Gawan** was its important member.
 
• He was made wazir or the prime minister and was given the title of **‘Khwaju-i-Jahan.’**
 
• The history of the Bahmani kingdom after this period is actually the record of the achievements of Mahmud Gawan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bahmani kingdom ruled between 1347-1526 AD.
 
• The Bahmani Kingdom was founded by Alauddin Bahaman Shah in the year 1347.
 
• He was also known as Hasan Gangu.
 
• The capital of the Bahmani Kingdom was Gulbarga.
 
• It was a Persianised Muslim state of the Deccan in South India and one of the major medieval Indian Kingdoms.
 
• Later, Ahmad Wali Shah shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar in the year 1424.
 
• Bahmani Kingdom reached its peak under the reign of Muhammad Shah III.
 
• The Kingdom stretched from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal, including the whole of Deccan.
 
• Rulers of Bahmani Kingdom
 
 
• Hasan Gangu Bahmani
 
• Muhammad Shah 1 (1358-1377 AD)
 
• Muhammad Shah II (1378-1397 AD)
 
• Feroz Shah Bahmani (1397-1422 AD)
 
• Ahmed Shah (1422-1435 AD)
 
• Muhammad Shah III (1463-1482 AD)
 
• Muhammad Shah III dies in 1482.
 
 
 
• After the death of Muhammad Shah III,, Bahmani Kingdom was divided into 5 kingdoms, namely
 
 
• Bijapur
 
• Ahmednagar
 
• Berar
 
• Golconda
 
• Bidar

questions.question: The Vijayanagar kingdom was established by _________ in 1336.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harihara and Bukka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vijayanagar kingdom** was established by **Harihara and Bukka** in** 1336**.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire, established in 1336, flourished in the **Deccan region of peninsular and southern India**.
 
• Founded by Harihara, also known as Hakka, and his brother Bukka Raya, the empire derived its name from its capital city, Vijayanagara, located in present-day Karnataka.
 
• **Vijayanagara district, **situated in the Indian state of Karnataka, lies within the Kalyana Karnataka region.
 
• It was established in 2020, emerging as the 31st district of the state after being carved out of Bellary district. The district's administrative center is Hosapete.
 
• Vijayanagara district encompasses the former capital of the illustrious Vijayanagara Empire, Hampi, which has been designated as a *UNESCO World Heritage Site*.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Venkatapati Raya,** from the Aravidu Dynasty, served as the third Emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire. He ascended to the throne following his older brother, Emperor Sriranga Deva Raya.
 
• **Deva Raya II **was a distinguished emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire, hailed as one of the most remarkable rulers of the Sangama dynasty. Known for his prowess in administration, warfare, and scholarship, he left a lasting legacy.
 
• **Krishnadevaraya, **a monarch of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1509 to 1529, was a prominent figure in Indian history. Belonging to the Tuluva dynasty, he is revered as one of the most illustrious rulers of India, renowned for his remarkable achievements during his reign.

questions.question: Who made the use of gunpowder common in North India to defeat enemies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Babur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur,** the inaugural ruler to adopt the title of 'Badshah,' heralded the widespread adoption of gunpowder and artillery in India following his triumphs.
 
• His conquests marked the integration of Kabul and Kandahar into the Indian empire, a feat unmatched since the era of the Kushanas.
 
• **"Gunpowder,"** a blend of saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal, gained prominence for its explosive propellant properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **As the progenitor of the Mughal Empire** in the Indian subcontinent, Babur traced his lineage to Timur and Genghis Khan through his paternal and maternal ancestry, respectively.
 
• Posthumously, he was bestowed with the epithet Firdaws Makani ('Dwelling in Paradise').
 
• Babur's demise in 1530, in Agra, prompted his son Humayun to ascend the throne.
 
• Initially interred in Agra, Babur's remains were later transferred to Kabul in accordance with his final wishes for reburial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ibrahim Khan Lodi,** succeeding his father Sikandar Khan Lodi, ascended to the throne as the final Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate in 1517.
 
• During Ibrahim Lodi's reign, **Daulat Khan Lodi **served as the governor of Lahore within the Lodi dynasty's administration.
 
• **Rana Sanga** held the distinction of being the last autonomous Hindu monarch in Northern India, governing a substantial domain before the onset of the Mughal Era.

questions.question: The ______ was a territorial assignment given to administrative officers and nobles in lieu of the services they performed for the state during Delhi sultanate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iqta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Iqta system 

 
 
• The Iqta system was a unique type of land distribution and administrative system introduced during the reign of Iltutmish.
 
• In the Iqta system the lands of the Delhi Sultanate were divided into several large and small tracts called Iqta and assigned these Iqtas to the Sultan's soldiers, officers and nobles.
 
• Iltutmish granted iqtas (land) to members of his army.
 
• Iqta is the land granted to army officials in lieu of a regular wage.
 
• The iqta holder is called the iqtadar or muqti who had to provide the Sultan with military assistance in times of war.
 
• 
 
The iqtadar collected revenue from his iqta to meet the cost of maintaining his troops and horses.
